Here the extra coordinate is read as an internal ladder inside a coarse site, and that reading is itself a price.\n47\t\n48\t## Lemmas\n49\t\n50\t**L1. Local self-energies relocate the mirror; they never remove it.** [proved, elementary; checked by T-F4-1]\n51\t\n52\tSetting:\n53\t- a finite-range Hermitian slab Hamiltonian H(k) on Z³ × {1..L};\n54\t- a far-wall self-energy Σ(ω) on finitely many layers that is independent of k, has any frequency dependence, and is Hermitian at ω = 0. Infinite eigenvalues are allowed and act as projections.\n55\t\n56\tArgument:\n57\t- After removing the infinite directions, h(k) = H(k) + Σ(0) is a smooth Hermitian matrix field on T³ of finite dimension.\n58\t- In each U(1) charge sector, its zero-eigenvalue points (poles of G(0,k), i.e. gapless states) have total index 0 (Stokes on T³).\n59\t- So the near Weyl's index χ is always matched by a gapless index −χ somewhere.\n60\t\n61\tScope:\n62\t- This covers atomic freezing (SPIN10's whole-layer and mirror-slot cases), DMFT- or SYK-type local self-energies, and any on-site far term.\n63\t- Any working far-wall mechanism must therefore produce a self-energy that depends on k and is singular at the mirror node.\n64\t\n65\t**L2. A successful far-wall gapping forces a non-kinematical zero.** [proved skeleton]\n66\t\n67\tSetting:\n68\t- the slab with a finite-range Hamiltonian, translation invariant along Z³, with an on-site U(1) (any U(1) ⊂ G_SM);\n69\t- a unique ground state;\n70\t- a near-wall Weyl with index χ ≠ 0 in charge sector q;\n71\t- no other gapless states of charge q (far wall and bulk gapped).\n72\t\n73\tClaim: for every finite-support interpolator set whose zero-frequency matrix G_q(0,k) is smooth and invertible away from isolated points or surfaces, G_q has zeros of total index −χ.\n74\t\n75\tProof skeleton:\n76\t1. G(0,k) is Hermitian at T = 0 by the Lehmann representation.\n77\t2. The negative-eigenvalue bundle of −G⁻¹ is smooth on T³ minus small balls, so the indices around the singular points sum to zero (Stokes).\n78\t3. Since the only pole is the near Weyl, some zero must carry −χ.\n79\t4. Enlarging the interpolator set cannot remove the zero, because a removed zero would need a new gapless pole, which is excluded.\n80\t\n81\tOpen steps:\n82\t- Luttinger surfaces instead of isolated points (handle by flux through enclosing surfaces);\n83\t- that the near Weyl shows up as a pole in the elementary near-wall field (true at weak near-wall coupling).\n84\t\n85\tConsequences:\n86\t- Condition 4 of Golterman–Shamir's generalized no-go (arXiv:2505.20436 §III: \"a complete set of interpolating fields exists so that R(p) has no zeros\") must fail in any successful slab gapping.\n87\t- Hence: the slab works ⇔ their \"zeros are kinematical\" conjecture is false for that model (they state the conjecture in arXiv:2505.20436 and its consequence in arXiv:2603.15985).\n88\t- With interactions at any strength, the slab is therefore exactly the place where the two camps make opposite predictions:\n89\t  - SMG camp: a protected zero;\n90\t  - Golterman–Shamir camp: a massless composite of index −χ appears, and the result is vector-like.\n91\t\n92\t**L3. Gauge-locality dichotomy for every inflow geometry without symmetric gapping.**\n93\t\n94\tSetting: the world is the boundary of a 4D region W carrying a C2 ≠ 0 insulator; on-site gauge invariance is exact; there is a light gauge field on the world. Three cases cover the bulk gauge links.\n95\t\n96\t- **(a) Dynamical, deconfined bulk links in a thin bulk (depth D).** [proved skeleton]\n97\t  - The light mode is constant along each fibre of W. It is a gauge field on the core M obtained by collapsing the fibres.\n98\t  - Each fibre's two boundary ends carry opposite chirality relative to M (Stokes along the fibre).\n99\t  - So the content is vector-like at gauge resolution. For the slab, M = world (near + far). For the folded slab, M = world/τ.\n100\t  - A thick bulk with deconfined links makes the photon 4+1D, giving Coulomb 1/r². That is excluded.\n101\t- **(b) Confining or Higgsed bulk links.** [suggested]\n102\t  - Moving a charged fermion through W costs a flux excitation.\n103\t  - Below that cost, the C2 band structure is gone, and each layer is a local 3D system, so NN applies.\n104\t  - Single-barrier toy: m_mirror ≲ (t/g)² m_γ²/M_Pl ≈ 10⁻⁶³ eV, against more than 10¹² eV needed (T-F4-2).\n105\t- **(c) Slaved bulk links** (gradient flow, harmonic extension, coarse-grained Wilson lines).\n106\t  - There are no bulk gauge degrees of freedom. But the bulk fermions are physical and have positive electric polarizability, so the bulk energy carries c ∫_W F_B² with c > 0.\n107\t  - This gives nonlocal photon terms:\n108\t    - flow: a mass-like plateau c/(2δt) for wavelengths shorter than √(Lδt);\n109\t    - harmonic extension into a deep bulk: a |k| kinetic term, i.e. Coulomb 1/r² beyond a few Planck lengths;\n110\t    - folded slab: a penalty of about c Φ²_strip/(2L) per site on the flux through world-sized strips.\n111\t  - The 1/L scaling is checked (T-F4-4b). The rest is suggested.\n112\t  - Euclidean domain-wall, Grabowska–Kaplan and Kaplan constructions avoid (c) with Pauli–Villars bulk subtraction. A unitary qubit Hamiltonian has no Pauli–Villars fields (reading).\n113\t- **Two-wall slab with Grabowska–Kaplan flow** (arXiv:1511.03649).\n114\t  - The mirror's Gauss-law charge is exact at every k, and its coupling is unsuppressed for k ≲ 1/ℓ_flow.\n115\t  - Required depth: L ≥ M_Pl/m_γ = 1.2 × 10⁴⁶ layers (light-cone recursion) or about 10⁹³ (diffusive flow) (T-F4-2, arithmetic checked).\n116\t\n117\t**L4. A thin single-boundary bulk must pair distant places.** [proved, using Smith theory, cited from memory and unverified this session]\n118\t\n119\tA thin W with connected boundary equal to the world is an I-bundle whose end-pairing τ is a free involution of the world. Every involution of R³ has a fixed point (Smith theory), and so does every finite-order lattice automorphism (by orbit averaging). Hence:\n120\t- the world must be compact, for example T³ with the glide (x, y, z) → (x + N/2, −y, z);\n121\t- τ moves some points by about half the world.\n122\t\n123\t**Dimension remark.** [reading] Lower-dimensional boundary-gapping successes are not evidence for 3+1D:\n124\t- in Fidkowski–Kitaev 0+1D end modes, the induced interactions are relevant;\n125\t- in 3-4-5-0 (1+1D), they are marginal;\n126\t- at d_surface ≥ 2+1, the order-t⁴/g³ terms that the strong-coupling expansion generates are irrelevant.\n127\t\n128\tGolterman–Shamir 2505 §V makes the same 2D/4D caution. Decisive tests therefore need surfaces of dimension 2+1 or higher.\n129\t\n130\t## Routes\n131\t\n132\t| Route | Family (object, mechanism, terminal obligation) | Premise dropped/changed | What you would have to believe | First artifact | Cost | What it would change if it worked |\n133\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n134\t| **A. Inflow slab, far wall gapped by interactions** | Z³ × ladder(L) per site; tuned 4+1D Wilson C2 = 1 insulator × 16 flavours per generation; G_SM ⊂ Spin(10) links shared across layers. Mechanism: inflow plus far-wall symmetric mass generation. Terminal obligation L_A: a symmetric, local far-wall interaction gaps the far wall (unique ground state) at intermediate coupling while the near 16 stays gapless. | A6 (no extra coordinate); A5 (free) at the far wall only; A2 (a site is a block of about 10³ qubits) | Far-wall symmetric mass generation exists with a *protected* zero (L2), i.e. Golterman–Shamir's kinematical-zero conjecture fails here | L1 and L2 (done); a pre-registered DQMC slab test (below) | Weeks of sign-free QMC for the 2+1D-surface version; months for the 3+1D 16 | The only local F4 construction: a full SM generation with no light mirrors, exact on-site gauge invariance, nearest-neighbour range, about 10³ qubits per site |\n135\t| **B. No-go for every F4 variant without interactions** | Any inflow geometry. Mechanism: Gauss law, collapse along fibres, positive polarizability. Terminal obligation: L3 | None (it is a no-go/price) | — | L3 plus T-F4-2 arithmetic (done) | Hours for the flow-plateau check (below) | Removes the flow/fluff, far-Higgs, layer-phase, record-depth ladder, folded-slab and disk variants under locality, so F4 reduces to A |\n136\t| **C. Folded slab (orientable twisted I-bundle, one connected boundary)** | T³ × [−L, L] / Φ, with Φ = (x + N/2, −y, z, −t) and spinor S = Γ2Γ4. Mechanism: topology (single edge) and evading NN by breaking one translation through the gluing. Terminal obligation: a gauge sector on W with no identification along fibres and no penalty from bulk polarization | A6; Lattice translation covariance and NN locality (one O(1) bond per site to the site τx half a world away); compact world | The owner accepts world-range nonlocal gluing **and** nonlocal photon terms, or a non-unitary bulk subtraction | T-F4-3 (PASS) and T-F4-4b (penalty ∝ 1/L), both done | Done | Shows that removing the mirror from the spectrum is cheap (2L layers per site). The wall in this family is gauging, not the spectrum |\n137\t\n138\t### Theorem-strength gap test\n139\t\n140\t**A, terminal lemma L_A.**\n141\t- L_A ⇒ T, given shared links, the anomaly-free 16 and three copies. The open steps are the gauge dynamics and whether the zero is harmless once gauged. A gapped far wall clusters exponentially, so its current response is analytic at q ≪ Δ and produces no ghost-like running (suggested). Golterman–Shamir (arXiv:2311.12790) argue the opposite, and this is unresolved.\n142\t- T ⇒ L_A. Any local chiral 16 can be stacked, as its conjugate, onto the far wall and paired with the mirror by symmetric bilinears.\n143\t- So L_A is **target-equivalent: blocked-equivalent.** The genuinely new mechanism over F1 (symmetric mass generation in 3D) has two parts:\n144\t  - mirrors are separated in real space rather than in momentum, so links cannot leak them (Eichten–Preskill);\n145\t  - L2 turns the existence question into a single observable: a protected zero, or a massless composite.\n146\t\n147\t**B.** Weaker than the target: a no-go for a class of constructions. It is an exact price, namely that F4 without interactions requires world-range nonlocality or at least 10⁴⁶ layers.\n148\t\n149\t**C.** By L3, the gauge obligation is equivalent to accepting nonlocality. It is priced, not open.\n150\t\n151\t### Price in framework terms\n152\t\n153\t**Route A** (per Z³ site, three generations):\n154\t- 3 × 16 × 4 × L fermion qubits (Jordan–Wigner) with L ≈ 4–6. At the tuned μ = 3, the near zero mode sits exactly on the boundary layer at k = 0 (layer centroid 1.0 in T-F4-1 and 6.0 in T-F4-3). That gives about 10³ qubits;\n155\t- plus the far-wall interaction sector: a Spin(10)-singlet quartic, or a Yukawa to a 10-vector rotor of about 4 qubits per generation;\n156\t- plus G_SM link registers, one set per Z³ link, shared across layers.\n157\t\n158\tSupplied structure that is not derived:\n159\t- fermion statistics;\n160\t- the internal ladder (a reading of what a \"site\" is; it is not the parked M₄(C) of DEFERRED #4);\n161\t- the Wilson Γ-structure and the μ ∈ (2, 4) tuning;\n162\t- the 16-flavour index and the G_SM embedding;\n163\t- which end carries the far-wall term, i.e. which hand is light (a sign bit);\n164\t- the far-wall interaction itself.\n165\t\n166\tAnomaly edge cases [reading; García-Etxebarria–Montero arXiv:1808.00009, Wang–Wen–Witten arXiv:1810.00844; not re-verified this session]:\n167\t- Per generation the 16 cancels the perturbative anomalies, the Witten SU(2) anomaly (4 doublets), and the Z₁₆ anomaly with Z₄^X (16 ≡ 0).\n168\t- Without ν_R and with Z₄^X kept, the anomaly is 15 ≢ 0 mod 16, so the far wall *cannot* be gapped symmetrically. The interaction must then break Z₄^X, or ν_R must exist.\n169\t\n170\tThere is no range price: everything is nearest-neighbour or inside a site.\n171\t\n172\t**Route C:**\n173\t- a compact world with an orientation-reversing free involution;\n174\t- an O(1) bond pairing every site with one half a world away;\n175\t- y-translation broken by the gluing;\n176\t- slaved gauge connections built from world-length Wilson lines;\n177\t- even then, the photon penalty needs L of roughly 10⁸⁹ (suggested, from c ≈ 5×10⁻³ and the photon-mass scale).\n178\t\n179\t**Owner decision touched.** The range question (`WALL.md:35`; `PRIOR_ART.md:232`). Inside F4:\n180\t- accepting world-range nonlocality is what buys chirality without interactions;\n181\t- keeping nearest-neighbour locality leaves only Route A.\n182\t\n183\t### Cheapest decisive tests (pre-registrable)\n184\t\n185\t**A.** A sign-free DQMC (Majorana QMC) of the 2+1D *surfaces* of a 3+1D topological-insulator slab, with interactions only on the far surface.\n186\t- Setup: surface content anomaly-free under the kept symmetry, e.g. 8 Dirac (16 Majorana) cones with a Slagle–You–Xu-type SO(4)/SU(4) interaction. Measure:\n187\t  - layer-resolved spectral weight;\n188\t  - the far-surface elementary G(0,k);\n189\t  - the far-surface composite (three-fermion) channel.\n190\t- Readings:\n191\t  - **PASS-SMG:** the far surface opens single-particle and composite gaps at finite U_c with no long-range order; the elementary G has a zero carrying the near cone's index; the near cones stay gapless (finite-size gap ∝ 1/L_x).\n192\t  - **FAIL-GS:** a gapless far-surface composite appears, or the near cones gap.\n193\t  - **FAIL-SSB:** a gap opens only together with long-range order.\n194\t  - **FAIL-RELOCATE:** gapless cones reappear one layer inward.\n195\t- This tests the mechanism one dimension below the target. It is the first dimension where the induced interactions are irrelevant.\n196\t\n197\t**B.** A free slab with flow-slaved links.\n198\t- Measure the bulk ground-state energy ΔE(k)/|A_k|² against the boundary field's wavevector k.\n199\t- Readings: **PLATEAU** if it tends to a k-independent constant for 1/√(Lδt) ≪ k ≪ 1 (this would confirm L3(c) for the flow); **NO-PLATEAU** otherwise. Cost: hours.\n200\t\n201\t**C.** Already run; see below.\n202\t\n203\t## Tests run\n204\t\n205\tAll readings were fixed in `TEST_PREREG.md` before each run.\n206\t\n207\t**T-F4-1** (`scripts/t_f4_1_slab_index.py`, outputs `t_f4_1_*`) — **LEMMA-CONSISTENT** (checked; an instrument check, forced by NN, as pre-registered).\n208\t- Free slab: near and far projected Chern numbers are −1 and +1, total 0.\n209\t- Far-layer Γ5 or Γ4 at λ ≥ 3: the mirror relocates to layer L−1 (centroid 3.0), still at zero energy.\n210\t- Random Hermitian far term: at λ = 0.3, a small pocket with total 0 inside ρ = 0.35. Plain words\n20\t\n21\t1. **The idea.** Put our world on one face of a thicker slab of qubits. The slab's interior is the kind of material whose surface carries one-handed particles. If the interior can be \"unknotted\" into a plain product state by a sequence of local steps that respect the forces' symmetry (a \"symmetric disentangler\"), then stopping the unknotting partway gives a far face with no particles on it at all, while the near face keeps our one-handed particles. The force fields can then be ordinary grid links shared by all the layers at a site. That would remove F4's force-side failure.\n22\t\n23\t2. **What it buys, honestly.**\n24\t   - **The force side does get fixed, but only by what the far face is made of** (proved skeleton). In the slab the symmetry already acts site by site. F4's failure was never that the symmetry was \"not on-site\". It was the opposite-handed copy on the far face.\n25\t   - **There is no way round a far-face interaction gap** (proved, given F4-L3). The disentangler does not avoid \"symmetric mass generation\" (SMG, interactions that gap the mirror without breaking the symmetry). It writes that interaction down exactly, as the disentangler sandwiching a trivial term.\n26\t   - **Whether such a disentangler exists is exactly as hard as the original wall** (target-equivalent, Lemma E). The physics core is already in the literature: Wang–Wen (PRR 2, 023356 (2020), arXiv:1809.11171) *assume* the needed statement.\n27\t\n28\t3. **What is new, and is it a new mechanism?** Not a new mechanism. It is a sharper map of the obligation:\n29\t   - In the slab, every lattice-level obstruction attached to *how the symmetry acts* is automatically zero (proved): Fidkowski–Xu, the Shirley–Zhang–Ji–Levin index, F3-B's κ, and the Tu–Long–Else lattice anomaly. So the qubit-sized-site worry is not an obstruction here.\n30\t   - The whole question is one statement about *a state*: the 16-flavour slab interior is trivial in the lattice classification of invertible states with the SM symmetry (S\\* below).\n31\t   - That statement and Golterman–Shamir's (GS's) conjecture cannot both be true (suggested).\n32\t   - No dimensional shortcut exists for the SM gauge group (proved by charge arithmetic). The Smith / decorated-domain-wall shortcut works only when the protection is a bare Z₄.\n33\t\n34\t4. **The test I could run** is in the one dimension where everything is computable: the time-reversal (T) Majorana chain, with 8 chains, i.e. 16 Majoranas per site. The near wall carries the 16_L and the far wall the 16_R mirror.\n62\t\n63\t### Terminal statement S\\* (the exact mathematical statement needed)\n64\t\n65\t> **S\\*(G):** there is a G-symmetric product ancilla state α and a locality-preserving unitary V, generated by a quasi-local, time-dependent, G-invariant fermionic Hamiltonian (so V is in the symmetric connected component, not merely a symmetric QCA), such that V(ψ₀ ⊗ α) is a product state. Sites are finite-dimensional.\n66\t\n67\tS\\* is **not** \"cobordism-trivial ⇒ the symmetry can be made on-site\", which is the TPF / Seifnashri–Shirley / SZJL form. In the slab the symmetry is on-site already. S\\* is a statement about an invertible **state**. Concretely it is:\n68\t\n69\t[cobordism invariant of ψ₀ = 0] ∧ [lattice completeness: invertible lattice states with zero cobordism invariant are symmetric-LPU-trivial].\n70\t\n71\t- The first conjunct is known: perturbative cancellation, Witten SU(2) and Z₁₆ all vanish for the 16 (comparator: García-Etxebarria–Montero arXiv:1808.00009; arithmetic re-checked in §5).\n72\t- The second is the open conjecture (Kitaev; Kapustin arXiv:1403.1467; Freed–Hopkins arXiv:1604.06527 for the continuum; recalled, not re-verified).\n73\t\n74\t### Lemma E (equivalence ladder; target-equivalence)\n75\t\n76\t| Step | Statement | Label |\n77\t|---|---|---|\n78\t| **E1: S\\* ⇒ H_DI** | Let V_{>w} be V's generator restricted to layers > w. So any local cure with on-site links needs the far content gapped G-symmetrically with no bilinear, which is SMG by definition.\n92\t\n93\tThe DI far wall is exactly that: H_far = V-conjugated sums of on-site trivial terms. The question's \"without far-wall SMG dynamics\" can only mean \"SMG made kinematic, exactly solvable, by V\", and V's existence is S\\*, which is target-equivalent.\n94\t\n95\t### Lemma O: on-siteness makes every symmetry-action obstruction vacuous (proved, by definition, plus checked arithmetic)\n96\t\n97\tIn the slab and in H_DI, G acts on-site: a tensor product over Z³ sites of unitaries on the payload. Hence:\n98\t- (i) Tu–Long–Else lattice anomaly = 0 (PRX 16, 011027 (2026), arXiv:2507.21209; abstract only);\n99\t- (ii) the SZJL index ω ∈ H²(G, ℚ₊) is trivial (arXiv:2507.21267; abstract only);\n100\t- (iii) every subgroup is depth 0, so FX's shallow-circuit condition is met;\n101\t- (iv) any U(1) that H_DI preserves must have Σχq = 0 on the near content (F3-B κ / anomaly matching). For U(1)_Y, U(1)_{B−L} and U(1)_X the sum is 0, but κ_F = 16 (checked, §5). So **V must break U(1)_F**, and that is the only constraint κ adds.\n102\t\n103\tThe finite-dimensional (qubit) worry in `OV:35-39` is a worry for **bulk-free** realisations (TPF's rotors). In the slab, finite dimension is automatic, at about 64L fermion modes per site per generation (F4's ~10³ qubits for three generations, `F4:153-156`).\n104\t\n105\t### What Fidkowski–Xu forbids (comparator plus reading)\n106\t\n107\t**Statement** (PRL 131, 196601 (2023), arXiv:2306.10105; abstract checked). With finite-dimensional sites:\n108\t- U(1)_A of a single Weyl cannot be a shallow circuit;\n109\t- a uniform chiral Z_{2N} on N_f same-helicity Weyl cannot be one when 2N ∤ N_f.\n110\t\n111\t**Here** (bulk-free H_DI after the product region is discarded; G on-site):\n112\t- FX forbids keeping U(1)_F;\n113\t- it allows Z₄^X at N_f = 16 (4 | 16) and forbids it at 15 (4 ∤ 15). This is the same verdict as the Z₁₆ anomaly (C1, `F1:63-83`).\n114\t- FX is weaker than the Z₁₆ anomaly in general (reading). It allows Z₄ at N_f = 4, 8 and 12, where Z₁₆ forbids it.\n115\t- **FX forbids nothing that the anomaly does not already forbid** for the SM 16.\n116\t\n117\t### Lemma G: V is necessarily non-Gaussian, and there is no dimensional shortcut for G_SM (proved, given the free classification and Read's theorem)\n118\t\n119\t- **(a) Gaussian part.** The only G_SM-singlet ψψ is ν^cν^c, which is Z₄^X-odd (checked §5). So every G_SM-symmetric Gaussian LPU conserves U(1)_F on the 15 charged components, and with Z₄^X on all 16. It therefore preserves the per-sector second Chern numbers of ψ₀, which are nonzero. **V must be non-Gaussian on every charged sector.**\n120\t- **(b) No 1D-style dimer factorisation.** V cannot be \"depth-1 non-Gaussian gates on disjoint blocks\" ∘ \"G-symmetric Gaussian LPU\". If it were, the Gaussian intermediate would be a product over finite blocks. Such a product has compactly supported Wannier functions and so carries no strong invariant in d ≥ 2 (Read, PRB 95, 115309 (2017), `OV:61`), contradicting C₂ ≠ 0. In 1D this factorisation *does* exist (T2 below), because 1D windings are compatible with compact Wannier functions. So the 1D mechanism provably does not lift.\n121\t- **(c) The Smith / decorated-domain-wall shortcut.**\n122\t  - **Bare Z₄ protection.** Ω₅^{Spin×_{Z₂}Z₄} ≅ Ω₄^{Pin+} = Z₁₆ would reduce 4+1D Spin-Z₄ triviality at ν = 16 to 3+1D DIII ν = 16 triviality. At the Gaussian level only ν^c can be trivialised, so the 15 charged components stay free-nontrivial and the reduction returns S\\*(G_SM, 15) itself (proved by (a)).\n124\t\n125\t### Lemma Z: S\\* needs bulk propagator zeros (proved skeleton; comparator Gurarie PRB 83, 085426, arXiv:1011.2273)\n126\t\n127\t- The 4+1D Green's-function winding N₅[G] is invariant along gapped paths on which G(0, k) has no zeros. It is 16 for ψ₀ (summed; nonzero per Y-sector) and 0 for a product state.\n128\t- So any path realising S\\* develops **bulk** zeros: the bulk analogue of F4-L2.\n129\t- **Reading/suggested.** If GS's \"zeros are kinematical\" conjecture also holds for gapped 4+1D bulks, where their condition (2) holds a fortiori, then N₅ with complete interpolators would be a path invariant, giving ¬S\\*. With Lemma O this sharpens F1-R3's corollary (`F1:126`):\n130\t  - GS true ⇒ there is a beyond-cobordism invariant of invertible **states**;\n131\t  - it cannot be an invariant of the symmetry action, because those all vanish here;\n132\t  - the only candidate in view is N₅ made rigid by kinematical zeros.\n133\t\n134\t### F4-C (folded slab) under X1 (reading)\n135\t\n136\t- Under S\\*, the folded slab is dominated: H_DI is local and single-faced, with no world-range gluing.\n137\t- Without S\\*, F4-C stays the only no-interaction single-face option, at its recorded price (`F4:136`, `:172-177`).\n138\t- Combining the disentangler with the fold adds nothing.\n139\t\n140\t---\n141\t\n142\t## 3. Every number and file reference is the worker's.\n26\t\n27\t## Plain words\n28\t\n29\t1. **The d-quark result was a choice of texture.** OBS-2's d-quark Lorentz violation (2×10⁻⁸ against 10⁻²²) comes from its Yukawa texture, not from CKM.\n30\t   - At one loop, a corner's speed shift depends only on the moduli of the corner couplings.\n31\t   - Quark mixing and CP violation live in the phases.\n32\t2. **The main construction (checked).**\n33\t   - Corner-basis Yukawa matrices for both sectors, with three equal diagonal entries and all six off-diagonal moduli equal.\n34\t   - With free phases, they reproduce every quark mass ratio, every |V_ij| and |J| exactly.\n35\t   - Every corner then sees the same speed shift. After the allowed per-field counterterms every row is zero: c̊ and d̊ for u and d, the anisotropic c⁽⁴⁾₃₃ rows next to them in D44 part 3, the heavy-quark rows and the electron rows.\n36\t   - This holds for every regulator, placement, symbol range and carrier model.\n37\t3. **The origin of OBS-2's residual.** OBS-2 gave each corner its own Yukawa coefficient, which breaks the law's cubic symmetry explicitly (OBS-2 REPORT:67).\n38\t   - If the law's couplings respect the cubic symmetry and flavour breaking lives only in electroweak-scale vacuum values, the symmetric-phase loops never see the flavour pattern, at any order (proved).\n39\t   - What remains is suppressed by about (v·a)², roughly 10⁻³⁴ (suggested).\n40\t4. **What CKM does force.**\n41\t   - The up and down embeddings cannot both be unbiased to the corner basis unless CKM is a disguised circulant (proved). The observed CKM is not one, at 31σ.\n42\t   - Some product of the two sectors' Yukawa matrices must carry corner-dependent data (proved).\n43\t   - If such products enter the velocity at two loops, the violation would return at about 10¹³ times the u/d bound (suggested estimate).\n44\t   - If the up sector is held flat and the corner couplings carry the mass pattern, there is no structural escape (proved). The fixed rows then vanish only on a hypersurface tuned to about 10⁻¹⁵.\n45\t\n46\t**Scope.**\n47\t- Physics: one loop; X2 walker on Z³ in continuous time; symmetric-phase nearest-neighbour Higgs; the family as built; no running from 1/a.\n48\t- Numerics: loop tables at N = 48 and 96; m0 = mH ∈ {0.1, 0.05, 0.025}; Δ ∈ {0, 0.5}.\n49\t- Variants covered: sym/int/ext placements; trace and selective splits; range-1 and range-2 symbols; carrier models M1 and M2; low-scale and ×0.45 Yukawas.\n50\t\n51\t## Reading (FIXED, TESTS.md:393-410)\n52\t\n53\t**TEXTURE-ESCAPE.**\n54\t\n55\t**The minimising realisation, \"B-gen\"** (`univ.out:10-45`, `univ_B_gen.npz`).\n56\t- **Fit:** exact, with χ² = 7×10⁻²³, all pulls ≤ 10⁻¹¹ and |J| = 3.116×10⁻⁵.\n57\t- **Moduli:**\n58\t  - |Y_u|/y_t: diagonal 0.3331, off-diagonal 0.3334;\n59\t  - |Y_d|/y_b: diagonal 0.3311, off-diagonal 0.3346.\n60\t- **Phases:** the off-diagonal phases are about 0.04–0.10 rad and depend on orientation.\n61\t- **Rows checked:** the as-printed D44 part-3 rows (u at 3×10⁻²³, d at 10⁻²²; Schreck 2017*, `ref_OBS2/paper.tex:10426-10441`) and the electron rows.\n62\t- **Result:** with universal data every residual is zero by Lemma S (proved, §1). Numerically, max |residual|/|universal shift| ≤ 6.8×10⁻¹⁴ over the whole bracket, all carriers and both symbol ranges (`univ.out:45,117`, `r2check.out:2`). That is roundoff.\n63\t\n64\t**Precision caveat.** The printed fixed-row \"ratios\" of 10²–10⁴ for these realisations are roundoff, not physics: double precision cannot resolve 10⁻²² against universal shifts of about 10⁻³. The zero is an identity.\n65\t\n66\t**A second universal fit, \"B-gen120\"** (diagonal phases spaced 2π/3), also fits exactly (`univ.out:82-117`).\n67\t\n68\t**The symmetric version fails** (checked over 400 starts; not proved impossible).\n69\t- Equal-modulus textures with symmetric off-diagonals, which is what on-site carriers give, cannot fit: the best χ² is 4.7×10³, with J only 1.2×10⁻⁷ and V_cb 0.010 (`univ.out:46-56`).\n70\t- This matches the USY literature: universal-strength textures fit the CKM moduli but not the size of CP violation (arXiv:1101.5808, abstract only).\n71\t- B-gen works because its phases depend on orientation. That needs orientation-selective τ_xσ_c carriers of range ≤ 2, which the family allows.\n72\t\n73\t## 1. Structure: what enters\n74\t\n75\t**S1 (proved).**\n76\t- Unit translations conserve the corner label, so the Lorentz-violating kinetic terms are corner-diagonal.\n77\t- The D2 subgroup fixing every hw1 corner makes each corner tensor diagonal.\n78\t- A mass eigenstate gets Σ_c |W_ci|² T(c,a) for left-handed fields, with |X_ci|² for right-handed ones.\n79\t\n80\t**S2, the one-loop formula (proved; symmetric phase, no carrier mixing).**\n81\t\n82\tT_L(c,a) = Σ_{s,s′} Re(η_s η̄_s′) I_{ss′}(c,a) + Σ_{c′≠c} w_{cc′} K(c,c′,a)\n83\t\n84\t- The η are the Higgs symbol coefficients. They are fixed only by the corner-diagonal entries Y_cc and the symbol choice: on-site part, selective, range-2 split.\n85\t- The weights are w_{cc′} = Σ_A |λ^A_{cc′}|² ≥ |Y_{cc′}|², by Cauchy–Schwarz with Σ_A v_A² ≤ v².\n86\t- Q sums the u and d sectors; u^c and d^c use the transposes, times 2.\n87\t- **Only moduli and the diagonal Gram matrix enter. The phases of the off-diagonal entries never do. This is the escape route.**\n88\t\n89\t**New exact identity (proved by q → q+Q plus σ_c spin conjugation; checked to 8.3×10⁻¹³ over N = 32–96 and the bracket, `structure2.out:1`).**\n90\t- For covariant on-site carriers, K(c,c′,a) = I₀₀(c′,a): the carrier loop equals the Higgs kernel of the internal corner.\n91\t- Hence T_L(c,a) = κ_⊥ (YY†)_cc + Δκ |Y_ca|².\n92\t\n93\t**When only (W y² W†)_cc enters.** In the on-site carrier class: a constant diagonal from the on-site Higgs, plus on-site covariant carriers at hw2.\n94\t- The per-corner isotropic part is exactly κ̄ (W y² W†)_cc, summed over sectors for Q; for right-handed fields it is (X y² X†)_cc.\n95\t- The per-corner anisotropic part sees the individual |Y_ca|², weighted by Δκ.\n96\t  - Δκ is 0 at Δ = 0, by staggered reflection (`structure2.out:2,4,6`).\n97\t  - Δκ is 2.2–3.8×10⁻⁴ at Δ = 0.5 (`:3,5,7`).\n98\t- In OBS-2's M1, the off-diagonals are not in the loop, so only Y_cc enters. With corner-dependent diagonals (selective symbols), their own kernels I_{cc′} enter.\n99\t\n100\t## 2. The cancellation condition and the conjecture\n101\t\n102\t**Lemma S (proved).**\n103\t- If the data are S3-invariant (the diagonal Gram matrix is invariant and all off-diagonal weights are equal), cubic covariance of the loop makes T(c,a) = α + βδ_ac. The residual is then identically zero.\n104\t- In the on-site class this is also necessary (proved algebra; generic Δκ, κ̄ ≠ 0): zero residual if and only if |Y|∘² = oJ + (d−o)·1, i.e. one common diagonal value d and one common off-diagonal value o.\n105\t\n106\t**Lemma F (proved).** After the speed counterterm, the isotropic row of eigenstate i is Σ_c (|W_ci|² − 1/3) ρ_c, where ρ_c is the per-corner isotropic residual and Σ_c ρ_c = 0. A flat column therefore has a zero isotropic row for any loop data.\n107\t\n108\t**The conjecture is proved in both directions:** W_u and W_d are both flat if and only if V_CKM is equivalent, under rephasing and permutations, to a circulant.\n109\t- **The elementary 3×3 step:** in a dephased Hadamard matrix, 1 + a + b = 0 with |a| = |b| = 1 forces {a, b} = {ω, ω²} (`algebra.out:4-5`).\n110\t- **Classification:** Haagerup 1997 (in *Operator Algebras and QFT*, Rome 1996, International Press, pp. 296–322); catalogue in Tadej–Życzkowski, quant-ph/0512154.\n111\t- **Forward direction:** V = D P F†(monomial)F P′ D′, a circulant times a monomial matrix.\n112\t- **Converse:** W_u = F P₁†D₁† and W_d = F C P₂ D₂ realise any circulant-equivalent V.\n113\t- **Prior art on main:** `QUARK_C3_CIRCULANT_SOURCE_LAW_BOUNDARY_NOTE_2026-04-28` (as cited by `CKM_SMALL_VS_PMNS_LARGE…NOTE_2026-06-06`). It covers the special case in which two Hermitian circulants give a permutation CKM.\n114\t\n115\t**The observed CKM is not circulant-equivalent (checked).** Such a matrix has a Latin-square moduli pattern. The PDG 2024 direct values (recalled) fail it:\n116\t- smallest entries of the rows: |V_ub| = 3.82(20)×10⁻³ against |V_cb| = 41.1(1.2)×10⁻³, a 30.6σ gap (`algebra.out:8`);\n117\t- middle entries: 152σ.\n118\t\n119\t**But the conjecture is not a lower bound.**\n120\t- **Realisation E1** makes both first-generation columns flat with the observed CKM: |W_u1|² and |W_d1|² flat to 10⁻¹⁶ (`escape.out:2`).\n121\t- **Its cost (checked):**\n122\t  - the heavy columns are then ≥ 0.283 from flat (`escape.out:1-2`);\n123\t  - the anisotropic u/d coefficients come out at about 10⁻⁴, failing the c⁽⁴⁾₃₃ rows by 10¹²–10¹⁷;\n124\t  - the u DIS row is reached at up to 1.2×;\n125\t  - charm and top isotropic shifts are ±1–2×10⁻³ (`escape.out:20-49`).\n126\t- So E1 escapes only the fixed rows, while B-gen escapes everything.\n127\t\n128\t## 3. Minimum over the family\n129\t\n130\t**Full family: minimum = 0, structural (proved; checked).** Three independent routes reach it:\n131\t- **B-gen and B-gen120:** all rows, both carrier models, any kernel.\n132\t- **M1 diagonal equalisation:** free right-handed rotations make the corner-diagonal Yukawas constant for any W_u, so every row vanishes in M1 (`univ.out:2-7`). This includes OBS-2's own branch-B left embeddings, W_u = F and W_d = FV. **OBS-2's −2×10⁻⁸ is removed by a d^c rotation alone.**\n133\t- **E1 (flat light columns):** fixed rows only, at the costs listed in §2.\n134\t\n135\t**Restricted to \"up sector flat\".**\n136\t- **Bounds (proved):** max_c ||W_d,c1|² − 1/3| ≥ 0.1206 (a scan gives 0.1221), and the b column is ≥ 0.0219 from flat (`algebra.out:18-20`, `upflat.out:1`). So the down-row sums are non-universal by at least 0.0219 y_b² (`structure2.out:8`).\n137\t- **M1:** minimum 0, structural (diagonal equalisation, `univ.out:2-3`).\n138\t- **M2** (the couplings carry the mass pattern): no S3-invariant realisation exists (proved), so there is no structural zero.\n139\t  - **On-site class.** The Q part of the d row is κ̄⟨δ^d, R^Q − R̄⟩, independent of the kernel. It changes sign over the generation phases (checked, `structure2.out:8`), so a zero needs tuning to about 2×10⁻¹⁵. The d^c part needs X_d1 to be flat together with a constant diagonal; that joint condition was not checked.\n140\t  - **Selective-symbol class.** Tuned zeros exist at single bracket points. Powell minima of the primary-point ratio are 0.04–4 (`upflat.out:8-13`).\n141\t  - **Best bracket-robust value found: 6.5×10⁹.** Powell is a local search, so this is an upper bound on the minimum, not a lower bound.\n142\t- **Conclusion:** within up-flat M2, the residual is CKM-forced unless tuned to about 10⁻¹⁵.\n143\t\n144\t## 4. Mechanisms outside the family's literal textures\n145\t\n146\t1. **A cubic-covariant law with flavour breaking only in vacuum values.** Proved for the symmetric-phase effective action at all orders.\n147\t   - Covariant couplings and propagators give U Σ(p) U† = Σ(Rp). So T is a cubic tensor field, and the residual is zero for any vev pattern.\n148\t   - This is consistent with X2-L8, which already puts the CKM-forced breaking in the vacuum.\n149\t   - Breaking enters only through vev insertions, at about y²(v·a)² ≈ 10⁻³⁴ for a = ℓ_P and about 10⁻²⁸ for a = 600 ℓ_P (suggested).\n150\t   - **Price, not computed:** the extra electroweak-doublet carriers at hw2 momenta have O(y_t) flavour-violating couplings, which raises a tree-level FCNC question (suggested).\n151\t2. **A Higgs degenerate at the corner-difference momenta.** By the K identity this is the same as the on-site carrier class. It produces the (W y² W†)_cc structure but is not an escape by itself.\n152\t3. **Main's velocity-RG attractor** (`EMERGENT_LORENTZ_INTERACTING_VELOCITY_RG_ATTRACTOR_NOTE_2026-06-06`, conditional). It gives only logarithmic suppression, not an escape.\n153\t\n154\t## 5. What CKM forces (companions to X2-L8)\n155\t\n156\t**L-words (proved).**\n157\t- If [H_u, H_d] ≠ 0, the unital *-algebra they generate is M₃ or M₂⊕C. Both contain a rank-1 projector onto a non-flat vector.\n158\t- So some word in H_u = Y_uY_u† and H_d has a corner-dependent diagonal.\n159\t- Any Lorentz-violating channel that resolves all such words with independent kernels is therefore forced to be non-universal by CKM.\n160\t\n161\t**Two-loop size (suggested).** The spread across corners of the words in B-gen (`structure2.out:10-16`):\n162\t\n163\t| Word | Spread across corners |\n164\t|---|---|\n165\t| H_u + H_d | 6×10⁻¹⁷ (zero) |\n166\t| H_u² | 1.6×10⁻⁵ |\n167\t| H_uH_d + H_dH_u | 4×10⁻⁷ |\n168\t\n169\tA two-loop coefficient of about κ̄² ≈ 1.3×10⁻⁴, projected through δ^u ≈ 0.3, gives about 10⁻⁹–10⁻¹⁰. That is about 10¹³ over the u/d rows, unless the couplings are law-level and covariant (mechanism 1).\n170\t\n171\t## Controls (all passed)\n172\t\n173\t- **OBS-2 reproduced.** c_TT^d = −2.10666612×10⁻⁸ and d_TT^d = +7.0222204×10⁻⁹ at N = 24, m0 = 0.1, Δ = 0, matching OBS-2's digits. OBS-2's referee obtained −2.10666629×10⁻⁸, a relative difference of 8×10⁻⁸. Δ = 0.5 also matches (`ctl.out:1-4`).\n174\t- **Circulant inputs** give residual/universal ≤ 2.9×10⁻¹⁴ in both M1 and M2 (`ctl.out:7`).\n175\t  - Side note: non-Hermitian circulants are only C3-invariant. Their per-corner isotropic residual is 6×10⁻¹⁶, but in M2 a transverse residual of 3×10⁻⁴ relative remains (`ctl.out:8`).\n176\t- **Cubic covariance:**\n177\t  - archived tables to 1.3×10⁻¹⁴ (`ctl.out:5`);\n178\t  - flavon table to 3.5×10⁻¹⁵ (`:6`);\n179\t  - assembly under the corner 3-cycle to 3×10⁻¹⁵ (`:9`);\n180\t  - range-2 tables to 1.2×10⁻¹⁴, with entries shared with OBS-2's tables identical (`r2_ctl.out`).\n181\t\n182\t## Deviations (all in PREREG_FOLLOWUP_2026-10-15.md)\n183\t\n184\t- **The u row.** The as-printed u row is 3×10⁻²³. TESTS says \"1e-22 as printed\", and the printed value governs.\n185\t- **Placements.** For right-handed fields the int and ext placements are swapped, a refinement of OBS-2's convention. The sym placement is unchanged.\n186\t- **Added after the PREREG:**\n187\t  - the M1 diagonal equalisation;\n188\t  - the equal-modulus fits;\n189\t  - the kernel identity;\n190\t  - the two-loop word diagnostics.\n191\t- **Bugs.** The C3b and r2check bugs were fixed before any reading.\n192\t- **Inputs not fetched.** PDG 2024 masses and CKM values were recalled, not fetched. The USY literature was read at abstract level only (Branco–Silva-Marcos–Rebelo 1990; arXiv:1101.5808; Kalinowski–Olechowski).\n193\t\n194\t## Files (`campaign/OBS3/`)\n195\t\n196\t- `PREREG.md`, `PREREG_FOLLOWUP_2026-10-15.md`.\n197\t- In `scripts/`:\n198\t  - `obs3_core.py` (assembly);\n199\t  - `ctl`, `escape`, `upflat`, `univ`, `structure2`, `algebra`, `r2check` (`.py` / `.out`);\n200\t  - `yuk_lv3.py` with `run_r2.sh` (range-2 tables);\n201\t  - `tables/`: OBS-2's tables plus the new `yuk3_*`;\n202\t  - `escape_E1_Wu.npy`, `univ_A_M1.npz`, `univ_B_{gen,sym,gen120}.npz`, `upflat_results.npy`;\n203\t  - `obs3_archive.npz` (63 arrays).\n204\t"}]},"uuid":"1920811b-4af0-4573-92dc-88b477bd3ad8","timestamp":"2026-10-17T11:06:27.425Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"93420ae5-99b1-46be-9d5d-9ebac274554f","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/jonBridger/Projects/Physics-baremetal-probes/.claude/worktrees/toe-leverage-analysis-e8a790","sessionId":"af5789b9-888d-43b1-90de-58a07e0f2129","version":"2.1.299","gitBranch":"claude/candidate-law-20261008","slug":"buzzing-crafting-pearl"}

{"parentUuid":"e1841541-0d06-4dbb-af28-0d0bf95c1540","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"63981d68-3e75-4c77-b96b-2e6c2b3a310b","agentId":"ab8e438892bdbfc5a","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FLw5bvs7MGU2hYBzTnWQ1s","type":"tool_result","content":"     1\t# Minimal Framework Axioms (Lattice, Qubit, Admissibility, Record)\n     2\t\n     3\t> **Key terms used in this doc** are indexed A-Z at `docs/KEY_TERMINOLOGY.md`;\n     4\t> each row points to the canonical source-of-truth doc.\n     5\t\n     6\t**Date:** 2026-06-29\n     7\t**Type:** meta\n     8\t**Status:** current public framework axiom memo for the qubit-on-`Z^3`\n     9\tpackage with local admissibility and fixed record readout.\n    10\t**Status authority:** explicit owner approval for the 2026-06-29 foundation\n    11\treset is recorded in `docs/audit/AXIOM_MINIMALITY_POLICY.md` section 6.\n    12\tAudit status remains set only by the independent audit lane.\n    13\t\n    14\t**Supersedes:** `MINIMAL_AXIOMS_2026-06-05.md`. The 2026-06-05 memo remains the\n    15\thistorical source for the prior Lattice/Quantum/Record wording in which\n    16\trealized outcome was latent in Record and no explicit local admissibility\n    17\tconstraint was named.\n    18\t\n    19\t## Purpose\n    20\t\n    21\tThis note states the framework's minimal ontology premises. They are named\n    22\trather than treated as bare letter codes:\n    23\t\n    24\t1. **Lattice**\n    25\t2. **Qubit**\n    26\t3. **Admissibility**\n    27\t4. **Record**\n    28\t\n    29\tLegacy `A1`/`A2` numbering and the older `Quantum` axiom name are historical.\n    30\tNew repo surfaces should use the axiom names above unless quoting an older\n    31\tdocument.\n    32\t\n    33\t## The Four Framework Axioms\n    34\t\n    35\t### Lattice / Physical Locality\n    36\t\n    37\tPhysical sites are the points of the cubic lattice `Z^3`, with nearest-neighbor\n    38\tadjacency, standard translations, and proper cubic rotations about each site.\n    39\t\n    40\tNo site is privileged. Sites are distinguished by the supplied lattice\n    41\tstructure alone.\n    42\t\n    43\t### Qubit / Site Possibility\n    44\t\n    45\tEach site has a domain of local possibilities.\n    46\t\n    47\tThe full one-site possibility domain has algebraic presentation `M_2(C)`.\n    48\t\n    49\tA `Cl(3,0)`-compatible real-algebra presentation may be used equivalently and\n    50\tadds no further primitive structure.\n    51\t\n    52\tNo possibility is privileged. One exploratory control run (W = 4, n_s = 4) reached 4.6e-3 and was discarded (follow-up C). | `validate_a_v2.out:6-10`; per-run \"max phase\" in `readout_final.out` |\n73\t| (iii) one finite-W observable agrees with an exact method | See below | `runs/gate3_dt005.log`, `runs/ed_gate3.log` |\n74\t| (iv) on even L, the light-corner G equals the free one | G(τ) = ½ **per configuration** to ≤ 1.8e-13, in every filtered run | \"max light dev\" column |\n75\t\n76\t**Item (iii) in detail.**\n77\t- Setup: reduced flavours (1 s + 1 c flavour, 4 d-modes per site, same channel builder and engine); 1D, L = 3, f1, W = 2, β = 2.\n78\t- At Δτ = 0.05, against ED:\n79\t\n80\t  | Observable | QMC | ED |\n81\t  |---|---|---|\n82\t  | W⟨Q⟩ | −0.1338(6) | −0.13438 |\n83\t  | Σ S | 0.5631(5) | 0.56382 |\n84\t  | E_kin | −2.4215(1) | −2.42148 |\n85\t\n86\t- Δτ = 0.1 also agrees within errors.\n87\t- Why not a Spin(6)/SU(4) version: the code path needs a real Clifford set of the Cl(9) type, and none exists for a 4×4 spinor.\n88\t\n89\t**Extra checks (checked).**\n90\t- The Fierz identity holds exhaustively on all 35,960 four-annihilator components (residual 1.0e-15, `x2model.out:3`). Under Wick contraction it holds to 1e-16 (`validate_a_v2.out:11`).\n91\t- The W = 0 Wick measurement agrees with ψ-frame ED to 1e-16 (`validate_a_v2.out:3-5`).\n92\t\n93\t## What was built (checked unless marked)\n94\t\n95\t**Frame.** SIGN-1's d-frame: a particle–hole transformation on 8_c, so every slice conserves d-number and commutes with T2 = (iσ_y ⊗ 1)K, where T2² = −1 (SIGN1 REPORT:62-72).\n96\t- Weight: det(1 + M_d).\n97\t- The referee's 1/√det M_d factor is constant here, because every HS generator is traceless.\n98\t\n99\t**Decomposition.** The pre-registered LP over the two-dimensional sign-correct Fierz family (`x2model.py:166-212`) chose κ = (sing8v +1.5, trip8v −0.5, 0, 0).\n100\t- That gives 64 HS channels per vertex, against 512 at SIGN-1's point.\n101\t- There is no remainder at λ1 = 0, because (Re P)² − (Im P)² = (P² + P†²)/2 exactly (proved).\n102\t- Each channel squares to ¼·1, so exp(zO) has a closed form.\n103\t\n104\t**HS fields and Trotter.**\n105\t- Each square has its own Gaussian field, so the HS step is exact.\n106\t- Vertex factors are ordered products, reversed on alternate slices (`afqmc.py:143-165`).\n107\t- The only systematic error is the Trotter splitting.\n108\t\n109\t**Vertex form (proved).** With F_x F_xᵀ = ρ·1, the vertex is 1 + F_xᵀ[(core − 1)/ρ]F_x.\n110\t- So a wrap costs O(taps·D·N_d) (`afqmc.py:179-216`).\n111\t- Updates are rank-32 Woodbury steps with 32×32 ratio determinants (`:256-294`).\n112\t\n113\t**Updates.** Preconditioned Crank–Nicolson moves of all fields at one vertex. They are reversible with respect to the Gaussian prior, so the acceptance is min(1, det ratio). The step size adapts during warm-up only.\n114\t\n115\t**Why not HMC (suggested).**\n116\t- HMC needs a stabilised forward and backward pass plus adjoint vertex derivatives at every MD step: about 6 N_d³ L_τ per step, 10–20 steps per trajectory.\n117\t- A local sweep costs about 2·acc·N_d³ L_τ.\n118\t- Measured τ_int(S10) is ≤ 1.3 sweeps for every f2 run (`runs/autocorr_final.out`; crude Sokal estimate).\n119\t\n120\t**Stabilisation.**\n121\t- Pivoted-QR UDV stacks every 0.4 in imaginary time.\n122\t- Stable G(τ) and G(τ, 0) come from one shared middle factor (`:241-254`).\n123\t- Wrapped-versus-fresh G deviation is ≤ 1.0e-8 in every valid run.\n124\t- Peak memory 0.99 GB, under the 1.5 GB cap.\n125\t\n126\t**det = |det_sector|².**\n127\t- **Not available** for the production decomposition: J does not commute with the triplet x, y channels (commutator 0.42).\n128\t- **Available in 2D** with the singlet-only Fierz vertex (sing8v 1.25, sing56v 0.25), which is also sign-correct.\n129\t  - J_d = (−1)^{x+y} σ_z ⊗ diag(1_s, −1_c) commutes with every slice (3.5e-17), and T2 J_d T2⁻¹ = −J_d.\n130\t  - So det(1+M) = |det(1+M₊)|², with half-size sectors.\n131\t  - Checked for f2 and f ≡ 1: the log dets agree to 1e-10 (`scripts/check_sector.out`).\n132\t- **Not available in 3D** with a J of this form, because no 2×2 matrix anticommutes with all three Paulis (proved for that form).\n133\t- The production runs were not switched to it.\n134\t\n135\t## Production results (checked; scope as above)\n136\t\n137\t**f2, 2+1D.** S10/N = S10/L². That mode remains untested.\n182\t\n183\t## Control against the literature\n184\t\n185\tThese comparators are from abstracts and search summaries only.\n186\t- **GPR**, 4D Eichten–Preskill SO(10) (K1:186-189): a symmetric massless phase, then an intermediate SO(10) → SO(9) broken phase, then a symmetric massive phase at strong coupling.\n187\t- **Slagle–You–Xu**, PRB 91, 115121 (2015), arXiv:1409.7401: DQMC on a bilayer honeycomb lattice; a direct transition from the Dirac phase to a fully gapped symmetric phase.\n188\t- **Ayyar–Chandrasekharan**, PRD 91, 065035 (2015), arXiv:1410.6474, and arXiv:1511.09071: staggered SU(4) with an on-site four-fermion term; massive without a bilinear condensate; a direct second-order transition in 3D.\n189\t- **He–You–Xu**, arXiv:2603.18278 (journal page PRB 114, 165125): direct SMG for SU(2)³; an intermediate excitonic phase in a Spin(5)×U(1) variant.\n190\t- **4D staggered results** (K1:190-193): narrow broken or antiferromagnetic intermediate phases.\n191\t\n192\t**Does the control reproduce known behaviour?** Only qualitatively (reading).\n193\t- Its sequence matches the GPR/EP history for this 10-vector channel: gapless, then gapped with large S10, then a strong-coupling regime where the uniform and staggered correlations fall.\n194\t- It does not reproduce a direct SMG transition. The direct-SMG models in 2+1D use different interactions, so this is no contradiction.\n195\t- At L ≤ 6 it cannot decide whether W = 0.25–0.5 is truly ordered, or whether W = 1 is truly symmetric. The ratios 0.79 and 0.86 lie between the ordered value (1) and the short-range value (about 0.44).\n196\t\n197\t## Cost model and gauge links (suggested)\n198\t\n199\t**Cost per 1000 sweeps per W point.** Calibrated as T = a·N_d³·L_τ on the measured 2+1D L = 6 sweep time (29.7 s with 2 threads; a = 4.86e-10). The cause is that the free partner has unpaired zero modes at the light corners: the same vector-like modes X2's T5 reported.\n- **Model B** (the registered threshold rule) keeps them gapless for κ ≲ 0.55 when W ≤ 10 W_c.\n- Which proxy is right is decided by L_X2's no-gapless-composite clause.\n\n### (iii) Observable changes\n\n| Effect | Source | Size | Against bound |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Dimension 3 (a-type): light energy split (1 new structure, count.out:1) | on-site density coupling to S | 3ε ≈ 1.2×10¹⁹ GeV at εa = 0.33, 1/a = M_Pl | ×4×10⁴² over IceCube 2.9×10⁻²⁴ GeV (bounds.out). Zero with Θ. |\n| Dimension 4 (c-type): flavour speed spread (3 new structures, not removable by OBS-3's two counterterms, count.out:2) | modulated walker hop η | 2η (light.out:33-37) | ×1.7×10²⁷ over IceCube 3.9×10⁻²⁸ |\n| The same, from the filter modulation | κ, through the hw3 admixture | ≈ κ²(1+O(κ)) (light.out:38-42) | ×2.8×10²⁶ |\n| The same, regenerated at one loop when the tree terms are set to zero | toy on-site pairing Yukawa y(x) = y₀ + y₁Σcos(K·x) | coefficient 0.147·(y₀−y₁)y₁ (loop2.out:2-5); spread 2.3×10⁻⁵ at a B-gen-like phase of 0.07 rad (loop4.out) | ×6×10²² |\n| Gauge couplings | — | unchanged: every mixing partner has the same G_SM charges, so the Ward identity fixes the charge (proved) | within bounds |\n| Light four-fermion terms, including ΔB = 1 (16⁴ ∋ qqql) | W(2κ)⁴a² | — | proton decay safe by 5×10⁷ at M_Pl, by ×10² at 2×10¹⁶ GeV (suggested) |\n\n## The price, with sizes\n\n1. **A named structure, Θ** (a lattice CPT, with S even under it). By AX:169-171, K/CPT structure is downstream of the axioms, so this is extra structure, not axiom content. Without Θ, the dimension-3 coefficient must be tuned to about 2×10⁻⁴³ (at M_Pl) or 1.5×10⁻⁴⁰ (at 2×10¹⁶ GeV).\n2. **Tuning.** Three new corner-off-diagonal c-type counterterm structures, probably needed per SM field (about 18; suggested). Each must be tuned to about 6×10⁻²⁸ of its tree-level natural size, or 2×10⁻²³–4×10⁻²⁶ of its one-loop size.\n3. **Conditions from (ii).** κ ≲ 0.55, and no gapless composite at the light corners. If such a composite does exist, κ must be ≲ 8×10⁻²⁹.\n\n**No part of the f range (fa ≥ 0.026) passes untuned** (bounds.out).\n\n## Comparison with the supervisor's own thread (read after all results)\n\n- **Agreed:** the BCC labels; single handedness per sector; the anomaly-free sector; unchanged gauge couplings.\n- **Wrong in the supervisor's thread:**\n  - Lemma S does not keep the zero. Cubic symmetry allows three corner-mixing structures that split the flavour speeds, and the loop regenerates them.\n  - θ goes into the composite partner, not into hw3, and the light modes couple at first order in κ.\n  - The supervisor predicted SAFE or a mild PRICE.\n\n## Deviations (`PREREG_FOLLOWUP_2026-10-15.md`)\n\n- The spin-density term P-b failed the cubic-symmetry check and was dropped.\n- The first direct-diagonalisation θ mixed degenerate zero modes. It was replaced by a degeneracy-safe measurement.\n- The count run hit the 0.4 GB cap because of a full SVD, and was rerun with an economy SVD. The killed log is kept.\n- Added after the PREREG: the literal model, the structure count, the one-loop toys and the index check.\n- The NT-3-style ED proxy was not run.\n\n## Scope\n\n- **Model:** 3D, continuous time, free-fermion one-body level per Spin(10) component.\n- **Mirror gap:** a static auxiliary partner, either at every site (Model A) or only in channels above threshold (Model B).\n- **Numerics:** folded-zone k-space, cross-checked against real-space tori with L = 4 and 6 to 3×10⁻¹⁴.\n- **One-loop work** is a toy: real iσ_y pairing, free internal lines, BZ grids N = 48–96, m_H = 0.05–0.1. No repository was edited and nothing was sent.\n\n**Path prefixes.**\n- CH = `origin/claude/chirality-grid-exercise-20261014:.claude/science/exercises/chirality-grid-20261014/`\n- AX = `docs/MINIMAL_AXIOMS_2026-06-29.md`\n- GR = `.claude/science/exercises/gravity-current-state-20261009/SUMMARY.md`\n\n## 0. Plain words\n\n1. **Putting one generation at each cube corner is what breaks X2's flavour sector. Its chirality mechanism is not what fails.** With exact grid translations, corner generations cannot mix the way quarks do. Every way to supply the mixing either fails flavour-changing bounds or needs tuning of about 1e-27. **Keep the mechanism; stop putting generations on corners.** The re-scoped package (call it X2′) puts all three generations at the one fully symmetric corner (k = 0) as an internal label. That removes four of the campaign's flavour prices by construction (suggested). The cost: the number 3 is supplied rather than explained, matter per site goes up ×3, and one Lorentz-violation price returns at one loop.\n2. **The Lorentz-violation part of every flavour price is the same wall as gravity's \"matter light cones\".** Its cost is set by gravity's open owner question on counting (GR:792), not by chirality. Jon should decide it once.\n3. **Route 1 is not closed.** The negativity sits in the part of the weight that does not depend on the measure. But no legitimate chiral measure has been tested on a geometry that can host one. Finish TOR-1, then stop route 1 in-house.\n4. **Route 3 should get referee time and the outside ask, not worker time.** Its decisive test is too large for this machine in 18 hours. Its question is exactly the one the outside SMG groups can answer from data they already hold.\n5. **QMC-1's validated code makes the collaborator ask timely now.** The compute is cheap (about $0.2k–$1k in the cloud for a 2+1D scan). What is missing is a specialist and a gap estimator the referee accepts.\n\n## 1. Verdicts\n\n### Q1. Route 2 (X2)\n\n**Is X2 viable?** It is not killed: every registered reading came back PRICE (CH/TESTS.md:362, :412, :468, :573). As registered, X2 is *flavour-priced out* unless Jon decides counting in its favour. Because main's hw=1 triplet programme reads generations off translation characters (`THREE_GENERATION_OBSERVABLE_THEOREM_NOTE.md:23-33`), **this is a cross-lane finding for the flavour lane**, like X2-L8 was for gravity.\n\n**Should X2 be re-scoped?** Yes (reading). What changes (all suggested; GEN-1 below checks them):\n- CKM is unconstrained by translations: Γ + Γ + 0 = 0, so F1, F2a and F2b do not arise.\n- Only the Standard Model's own FCNC remains.\n- The Γ label sector is single-handed, and f(Γ) = 0, so X2-L1 and X2-L2 survive.\n- Γ has full cubic symmetry, so no first-order traceless-strain channel exists (F4 removed).\n- The light content is translation-neutral, so X2's mixed-Z₂³ kill question should pass automatically.\n- Light³·mirror couplings become translation-forbidden.\n\nWhat it costs:\n- the native \"3\" (now a supplied index);\n- 96 complex modes per site instead of 32;\n- **no texture escape for one-loop Lorentz violation.** The speed matrix on Q is ∝ H_u + H_d, and that cannot be flat in both the up and down bases.
